title: King VII Crosses East
text:
Orun Vhal crossed the eastern border alone.

The army remained behind him.

That was deliberate.

He wanted to see what Vaelor had failed to conquer.

Kael met him first.

Not as a duel.

As a warning.

[[speaker:kael]]“Turn back.”

Orun looked at the mountain behind Kael.

Touched the ground with one toe.

[[speaker:orun]]“This land is young.”

Kael attacked.

Unmoving Heaven landed cleanly.

Orun moved half a step.

That was all.

Then he released force he had deposited into the road during his approach.

Kael was struck from beneath by three separate impacts.

One from ten steps ago.

One from twenty.

One from a hill he had crossed that morning.

The Buried Sovereign did not merely fight where he stood.

He fought from everywhere he had already been.

title: Kael Learns the First Rule
text:
Kael survived Orun's first engagement.

He did not win.

The important discovery was simple:

Never fight the Buried Sovereign on ground he has walked before.

Unfortunately, Orun had crossed half the western border by then.

Every road became suspect.

Every bridge.

Every courtyard.

Every mountain pass.

Jin ordered entire regions evacuated without explaining why.

People complained until one abandoned fortress detonated six hours after Orun left it.

No enemy inside.

No trigger visible.

Just stored force released remotely.

Jin stopped receiving complaints.

Ancient King VII had weaponized geography itself.

title: The First Coalition
text:
Kael refused to fight Orun alone again.

Liang joined him.

So did Rui.

Ilyra arrived with Mo and Arin under strict orders not to engage directly.

Orun smiled when he saw the formation.

[[speaker:orun]]“Better.”

The battle lasted nine minutes.

Rui continuously replaced terrain with moving water so Orun could not store stable force.

Liang redirected impacts away from organs.

Kael controlled centre.

Ilyra protected the Marquises and cut Orun's secondary routes.

They finally pushed King VII backward.

One step.

Then Orun released force stored inside the mountain from centuries before any of them were born.

The cliff behind the coalition exploded.

Everyone understood at once.

He had been here before.

Centuries ago.

title: Buried Heaven
text:
Orun's coronation legend had been incomplete.

He had not merely stored force for seven years in one capital.

He had travelled his entire kingdom doing the same.

Centuries of footsteps.

Centuries of pressure.

Centuries of strikes buried inside terrain.

His Ancient Art was finally recorded by Jin:

**BURIED HEAVEN.**

Jin's first description was still incomplete.

Stored impact was only the visible half of Orun's cultivation.

His true foundation was **EARTH BURIAL**.

Natural earth, stone, dust and sand were not scenery to him. They were extensions of his martial body.

Orun pressed his palm downward.

The valley floor fractured into powder.

Rock became grit.

Grit became a moving brown sea.

**ANCIENT ART — SANDSEA FUNERAL.**

Every grain carried a splinter of force Orun had buried in the valley over centuries. A footstep disturbed hundreds. A movement technique disturbed thousands. The coalition suddenly found that simply crossing the battlefield meant being struck from every direction by impacts too small to block individually and too numerous to ignore.

Kael hit Orun cleanly.

The King's body moved.

The surrounding cliffs cracked instead.

Jin understood the second principle.

**ANCIENT BODY ART — EARTHBOUND KING.**

While Orun remained connected to natural ground, part of the damage inflicted on him could be transferred into the earth itself.

Buried Heaven was not an isolated trick.

The entire landscape was his second body.

Orun could make history itself attack.

The coalition retreated before the entire valley became a weapon.

Kael hated retreating.

Jin did not.

[[speaker:jin]]“Living is strategically useful.”

Kael looked at him.

[[speaker:jin]]“You should try it more often.”

The Seventh Army did not follow Orun toward the ranking strongholds.

It turned south.

Thirty thousand western infantry moved toward the Riverglass evacuation road, where three provinces were trying to move civilians behind the second defensive line.

Mo Qingzhao reached the road first.

World #7 did not challenge the army head-on.

He opened a blank scripture over the canyon and wrote one sentence across the sky.

**TRANSCENDED ART — TEN THOUSAND PAGES BURY THE SKY.**

Every military order shouted beneath the scripture appeared on a different page.

Mo read the army's command structure faster than its officers could change it.

He did not destroy thirty thousand soldiers.

He made thirty thousand soldiers receive contradictory marches, false retreat horns and bridge orders that had never been given.

By sunset, the evacuation column was twelve miles away and the Seventh Army was still trying to discover which commands belonged to its own generals.

Mo closed the scripture.

[[speaker:mo]]“I prefer armies. They contain paperwork.”

title: Ilyra Protects a Duke
text:
Lei arrived late and angry.

He attacked Orun's convoy before the others could stop him.

Thunder struck the road.

Orun released stored force through the conductive stone.

Lei's own battlefield turned against him.

One buried impact broke his stance.

A second came from behind.

Ilyra reached him first.

Twin Meridian Scripture split.

One half caught Lei.

The other absorbed the next impact through a sacrificial circulation loop.

Both of them crossed the road violently.

Lei stared at her.

[[speaker:lei]]“You protected me.”

[[speaker:ilyra]]“You were about to die stupidly.”

[[speaker:lei]]“Still counts.”

She hated that he was correct.

title: The First King Is Driven Back
text:
Jin stopped trying to defeat Orun.

He changed the objective.

Force King VII away from natural earth entirely.

Rui created a temporary battlefield over a lake.

No natural earth beneath his feet.

No old stone.

No road carrying buried history.

More importantly, nothing for Earthbound King to transfer damage into.

Kael and Liang drove Orun toward it.

Ilyra protected the Marquises controlling the perimeter.

Orun stepped onto the water.

Buried Heaven had nothing stored beneath him, Sandsea Funeral had no material to claim, and Earthbound King lost its natural anchor.

Kael hit him.

Liang followed.

Rui collapsed the entire water field around his body.

Orun still did not fall.

But he finally bled.

One drop.

The East celebrated far too early.

title: King VI Walks an Old Road
text:
A man appeared inside Jin's command fortress.

No guards saw him enter.

No wall had been breached.

He simply stepped out of an empty corridor.

**Iscaryn Voss. Ancient King VI.**

The Thousand-Road King.

Two centuries earlier, Iscaryn had walked every major road of the western world as a nameless challenger.

He became King after seven enemy capitals were attacked in one night despite being separated by impossible distances.

The truth was stranger.

He had walked those roads before.

Once Iscaryn traversed a route, his cultivation remembered it forever.

**Every Road Returns to Me.**

Jin looked at the corridor behind him.

The fortress had been built thirty years ago.

Iscaryn smiled.

[[speaker:iscaryn]]“The road was older.”

title: No Fortress Is New
text:
Iscaryn did not kill Jin.

That frightened him more.

The King walked through the command fortress, touching nothing.

Then disappeared through another remembered route.

Jin ordered the foundations excavated.

Beneath them was an ancient stone road.

Buried for six hundred years.

Iscaryn had walked it.

The implication spread quickly.

Modern cities had been built over old roads.

Palaces over old roads.

Ranking halls.

White Court.

Even villages.

Anywhere Iscaryn had travelled in centuries past could become an entrance.

The East no longer had a secure rear line.

Ilyra read the list of dead Crowns alone.

Aurel.

Valeria.

Sorin.

Names that had once occupied the same halls she had abandoned.

She had survived because she stopped being Crown II before Orun began hunting western identities.

That fact did not feel like luck.

It felt like accusation.

She removed the eastern #6 tablet from her belt and placed it beside the old Crown insignia she had kept hidden for years.

One identity had saved her by being discarded.

The other had been given to her because someone else retired.

For the first time since joining the East, Ilyra wondered whether every number she wore belonged to somebody who had left first.

title: Orun Smiles at the Wrong Time
text:
Orun returned to the lake battlefield.

This time prepared.

He had stored force in pieces of stone carried inside his clothing. Portable earth could preserve Buried Heaven, but it could not reproduce the vast damage-sharing body of natural terrain.

Jin swore audibly.

The Buried Sovereign released them.

Kael blocked one.

Liang two.

Ilyra took a third meant for Mo.

Then a road appeared in midair.

Not physically.

A remembered route.

Iscaryn stepped from it and struck Kael from an angle no map contained.

Two Ancient Kings.

One battlefield.

The coalition broke immediately.

Orun smiled.

The East realized the Seven Kings were willing to cooperate.

That had not been in any surviving legend.

title: The Wrong War
text:
Jin stared at the battle map until dawn.

Two Kings had appeared.

Five remained.

The armies were still advancing behind them.

Kael injured.

Liang injured.

Lei injured.

Rui exhausted.

Ilyra carrying half the Marquis protection burden herself.

This was not a sequence of duels.

It was an invasion.

The Kings did not care about giving the East fair fights.

That realization changed everything.

Jin sent one message to every ranked fighter:

STOP CHALLENGING THEM.

SURVIVE THEM.

Somewhere far away, Sera was arguing with Rhen about tea prices.

The East did not know where to find them.

Not yet.

 

Far away, Sera was closing the tea shop when one of Jin's old emergency birds landed on the windowsill.

She had told him not to send those anymore.

The bird looked exhausted enough that she forgave it.

Rhen continued washing a cup.

Sera read the casualty figures once and folded the paper.

[[speaker:rhen]]“You want to go.”

[[speaker:sera]]“I want everyone to stop finding new ways to almost die.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“Different sentence.”

She glared at him, then rested her forehead between his shoulder blades.

For a while neither moved.

Rhen reached back and covered one of her hands with his.

[[speaker:rhen]]“If you decide to return, I will not stop you.”

[[speaker:sera]]“That is annoyingly supportive.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“I can be less supportive.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Don't.”

The bird remained on the sill.

Sera did not answer Jin that night.

But she did not burn the message either.
